retraction.reason: Re-read on 24 September under A14(6) against the rule that replaced M44b's. A record earns its place by carrying at least one honest edge to anything already in the atlas, and nobody writes an edge in order to keep a record. The corpus is now 859 active events across all five lanes, where M44b judged this one against the Portuguese core alone. The second reason M44b gave stands, and it is not the Portuguese rule. The item describes twenty-two years of policy under several headings rather than an event, and a record dated 1930 that runs to 1952 cannot take an edge that means anything at either end. The atlas now holds molotov-ribbentrop-pact and the Soviet records around it, so the neighbours exist. What is missing is a record of a datable thing to wire them to. Somebody would have to divide this record before reinstating it, the way this same day divided the Holocaust.
